business_problem: Ajuntament de L'Hospitalet needed to replace an aging storage platform that was creating performance and availability risk for resident-facing digital services, while minimizing disruption to mission-critical municipal operations during the transition.
solution_summary: The city council modernized its core storage layer with IBM FlashSystem 5200 arrays powered by IBM FlashCore modules, deployed with partner Logicalis Spain alongside an IBM Storage Networking SAN64B-7 switch. The implementation spanned both mainframe and open systems environments and used IBM HyperSwap to convert the existing VMware estate into a stretch-cluster architecture. That gave the municipality an active-active design with automatic failover instead of a more fragile single-site setup. More than 150 virtual machines, including application servers, databases and domain controllers, now run on the upgraded environment, which also layers in hardware-based compression, built-in FIPS 140-2 encryption, immutable backups and anomaly detection. In practice, IBM became the shared storage and resilience fabric for internal council systems and the external 24x7 resident portal, combining better latency with operational continuity and stronger data protection.
